h1: 4 Ring Gas Burner with Mild Steel Stand for Large Sufurias
short_description: Cooking for a crowd should not mean waiting an hour for water to boil. This 4 ring gas burner puts four powerful flame rings under one big sufuria, so ugali, githeri and stew for hundreds of people are ready faster, with less gas wasted. The low, heavy mild steel stand holds a full pot safely, making it the go-to burner for schools, hotels, churches and caterers across Kenya.

sections.heading: Key Features and Benefits
sections.body:
Four flame rings, four separate brass valves. You control exactly how much heat goes under the pot: one ring to simmer and keep food warm, all four for a fast, rolling boil. That means faster meals at peak times and less gas burned the rest of the day.

A wide flame across the whole base of the pot. Heat reaches the edges, not just the centre, so big batches cook evenly and the bottom is less likely to burn. Your cooks spend less time scraping and stirring.

A low, heavy mild steel stand with a grid top. A full, heavy sufuria sits level and secure, and the top of a tall pot stays at a comfortable stirring height. Safer for your staff and easier on their backs.

Tough, repairable build. Welded mild steel takes years of knocks in an institutional kitchen and can be repaired easily, so your investment keeps paying back.

sections.heading: Who It Suits and Where It Is Used
sections.body:
This burner is made for bulk cooking. It suits school and college kitchens, hospitals, hotels, restaurants with large daily batches, event caterers, and outdoor cooking for weddings, funerals and church functions.

It also works well beside an existing commercial cooker, taking the biggest pot off the main range so the other burners stay free for smaller dishes.

sections.heading: How It Compares with a Standard Cooker
sections.body:
A normal 2 or 4 burner cooker spreads its heat across several small burners, and a large sufuria placed on one of them heats slowly and unevenly. This 4 ring gas burner puts all its heat under one pot. The flame covers more of the base, so big volumes reach the boil sooner and cook more evenly.

The four valves also give you more control than a single large burner. Light the inner ring for slow cooking, then open the outer rings when you need full power. Using only the rings you need also helps you save gas over a long cooking day.

sections.heading: What to Check Before Buying
sections.body:
Confirm that you have a suitable gas supply, regulator and hose for a multi-ring burner, and that the cylinder size matches how long you cook each day. Measure your largest pot so it sits fully on the frame.

Place the burner on a level, non-flammable floor with good ventilation and enough space around it to work safely. Indoors, a kitchen hood or open air flow is recommended.

sections.heading: Care and Maintenance
sections.body:
Let the burner cool, then brush off food spills and soot from the rings so every port lights evenly. Wipe the frame and keep it dry to protect the mild steel finish.

Check hoses and valve connections regularly with soapy water and replace any part that shows a leak or cracking. Close every valve and the cylinder after each use.

sections.heading: Why Aluminium for a Big Sufuria
sections.body:
Aluminium is lighter than stainless steel of the same size, which matters a lot when a pot holds 100 litres. An empty pot is easier to wash, carry and store, and a full one is a little easier for two people to lift.

sections.heading: Key Features and Benefits
sections.body:
Electric heating, no gas. There is no cylinder to refill or open flame near the oil, which makes the fryer safer and cleaner to run, and it fits buildings where gas is not allowed.

Accurate thermostat with indicator lights. Set the temperature once and the fryer holds it, so every batch comes out crisp and evenly cooked. Correct temperature also means food absorbs less oil and your oil lasts longer, which saves money every week.

sections.heading: Why Choose an Electric Fryer
sections.body:
Electric fryers are popular in Kenyan kitchens because they are clean to run and easy to control. There is no gas cylinder to refill or move, and no open flame close to hot oil, which makes the kitchen safer for staff.

The thermostat holds the oil at the temperature you set, so each batch of chips or chicken comes out the same. Stable temperature also means the oil breaks down more slowly, so you change it less often and save money over time. A floor-standing fryer on its own stand also frees your counters for preparation and serving.

sections.heading: What to Check Before Buying
sections.body:
Check that your electrical supply can carry the fryer's load, and use a dedicated, properly rated socket or connection. Ask an electrician if you are unsure whether your premises are single-phase or three-phase.

Plan the floor space for the stand, with room to lift the basket and drain safely. Keep the fryer away from water and sinks.

sections.heading: Care and Maintenance

Switch off and let the oil cool completely before draining or cleaning. Filter or change the oil regularly and remove crumbs from the tank so they do not burn.

Wipe the stainless steel body and stand with a mild detergent and a soft cloth. Keep the control panel dry.

h1: Stainless Steel Batch Milk Pasteurizer with Agitator
short_description: Turn raw milk into safe, higher-value milk that customers trust and regulators approve. This stainless steel batch milk pasteurizer heats milk evenly with a motorised agitator and shows the exact temperature on a digital display, so every batch is pasteurized properly. It is built for dairies, milk ATMs, farmer groups and yoghurt makers across Kenya.

sections.heading: Key Features and Benefits
sections.body:
Hygienic stainless steel tank. Stainless steel does not taint milk, resists corrosion and is quick to clean and sanitise between batches, which protects your product and your licence.

Motorised agitator. Constant stirring spreads heat evenly, stops milk scorching on the bottom and makes sure every litre reaches the same safe temperature. Better taste, fewer losses.

Digital temperature display and simple controls. Your operator can see the temperature at a glance and time the holding period correctly, giving consistent, safe milk without guesswork.

Bottom outlet valve. Drain milk straight into cans, a chiller or a dispenser without lifting the tank, which saves time and reduces spills and contamination.

sections.heading: Who It Suits and Where It Is Used
sections.body:
A batch pasteurizer suits small and medium dairies, farmer cooperatives, milk bars and milk ATM operators, yoghurt and mala producers, schools and institutions that process their own milk.

Pasteurizing in your own premises lets you sell safer milk, extend shelf life and add value to raw milk from your farm or suppliers.

sections.heading: How Batch Pasteurization Works
sections.body:
Raw milk is poured into the tank and the lid is closed. The milk is heated while the agitator keeps it moving, until it reaches the pasteurizing temperature shown on the digital display. It is then held at that temperature for the required time to kill harmful bacteria.

After the holding time, the milk is drained through the outlet valve and cooled quickly, either in a milk cooler or by another cooling method, before it is packed or dispensed. Processing in batches gives small businesses full control of each lot of milk and makes it easy to adjust volumes from day to day.

sections.heading: What to Check Before Buying
sections.body:
Confirm the daily volume you plan to process so you choose the right tank size. Check your power supply for the motor and controls, and plan for a water supply and drainage for cleaning.

If you will sell milk to the public, check the current Kenya Dairy Board requirements for your premises and equipment before you start.

sections.heading: Care and Maintenance
sections.body:
Clean the tank, agitator and outlet valve after every batch using a dairy-safe detergent, then rinse and sanitise. Never leave milk residue in the tank.

Keep the control box and motor dry during washing. Check the agitator and valve seals regularly and replace worn parts.
